newsitem.title: USA: General Scanning Q4 shr $0.18 vs $0.14.
newsitem.headline: General Scanning Q4 shr $0.18 vs $0.14.

text.p: Three months ended Years ended December 31,
For the three months ended December 31, 1996, General Scanning's sales totaled $40.0 million, an increase of 13 percent over $35.5 million in sales in the fourth quarter of 1995.

Laser systems and component sales increased 12 percent to $33.3 million from $29.7 million in the comparable period of 1995, primarily due to sales of laser imagers for applications in diagnostic medical imaging and commercial graphics.
Thermal printer sales increased 17 percent to $6.8 million from $5.8 million in the comparable period of 1995, primarily due to the introduction of a customer's new product.

Income from operations increased 41 percent to $3.6 million, or nine percent of sales, for the three months ended December 31, 1996 from $2.6 million, or seven percent of sales, for the comparable period in 1995.

Net income after tax was $2.2 million, or $0.18 per share based upon 12.5 million common and common equivalent shares outstanding, compared to $1.7 million in net income, or $0.14 per share based upon 12.3 million common and common equivalent shares outstanding in the fourth quarter of 1995. An abnormally high tax rate was applied to the results in 1996.

(both quarterly and for the year) due to: (i) a portion of the merger expenses not being tax deductible and (ii) losses incurred at View prior to the effective date of the merger could not be used to offset General Scanning's profits for tax purposes.

For the twelve months ended December 31, 1996, General Scanning's sales totaled $156.5 million, an increase of 24% over $126.3 million in sales for the year 1995. Laser systems and component sales increased 28% to $131.9 million from $103.4 million in the comparable period in 1995.
Thermal printer sales increased 8% to $24.7 million from $22.9 million in 1995.
Income from operations increased 79% to $13.8 million, or 9% of sales, for the year ended December 31, 1996 from $7.7 million, or 6% of sales, for the comparable period in 1995.

Net income after tax increased by 44% to $6.6 million, or $0.53 per share based upon 12.5 million common and common equivalent shares outstanding. This compared to $4.6 million in net income, or $0.44 per share based upon 10.4 million common and common equivalent shares outstanding in 1995. The increase in shares was primarily due to the Company's initial public offering of approximately 2.6 million shares of Common Stock in late September 1995. Net income for 1996 includes one-time merger expenses of $1.95 million and an effective tax rate of 45% compared to 38% in 1995. Earnings per share excluding one-time merger expenses and taxed at 1995's tax rate would have been $0.69.
Backlog at December 31, 1996 was approximately $36 million compared to $42 million at December 31, 1995.
